shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares, using the anchor name of the node that owns the thing (envelope and cas from N-01, record-kinds-registry from N-18, codes from N-43, break-glass from N-27). check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for stats.rendered 200; counters.written 201; counters.invalid 422; counters.failed 500; stats.stale 503; counters.timeout 504. Owner-acts: counters.failed after three skipped ticks (one card).
A lamp column per code (green, amber or red) so a screen draws a code without a table of its own; N-37 generates bindings from it and the stats legend takes its chip colours from it.

The counters view the Go service computes every tick over the records table for four windows (1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d) and the previous window of each, keyed by window plus tick minute: tickets per stage (cut, started, tested, reviewed, merged), seat bring-up seconds median and p95, stalls per node, records per kind, jobs, wakes, seats, pods, cost; one writer, a lower-at frame dropped.
The record envelope every kind carries: id, at (UTC), code, kind, node, attempt where one applies; this node reads and writes records only inside it.
idempotency(key PRIMARY KEY, seq, response JSON, at); a seen key replays its response with code 200.

The record kinds registry (every kind with its code set, writer node and schema path, loaded by N-43 with the code table) carries the kinds this node reads and writes: counters.frame (N-31), rail.panel (N-33), tick (N-06); stats.frame is drawn and never stored.
records(seq, id, at, code, kind, node, ticket, attempt, body, hash): every count on this screen is a count over record kinds in this table, never a tally a seat maintains.
ticks(at, kind, duration_ms): the tick minute that keys a counters window and the skipped-tick count that becomes counters.failed.
The rail panel (plan steps done of total) is a record the system writes, shown here as one panel; this node never reads the plan file.
No cog: every wait has a timeout and a fallback, nothing starts by an agent typing, no agent is a gate; the system drives (brief C rule 3).
Many agents at once from the first line: append-only records, compare-and-swap, idempotent retryable steps, conflicts that report as 409 (brief C rule 2).
Every automated step retries up to 3 times with backoff, then recovers and reports as a record; a dead record becomes exactly one card.
One store, no broker: the counters view is a query over the one SQLite store, never a second metrics database.

purpose.s: Production statistics for the line: tickets cut, started, tested, reviewed and merged per window; seat bring-up time against the design bound; stalls per node; records, jobs, wakes, seats, pods and cost; rail progress (wireframe-brief.json screen Stats; C32 approved). Primary action: change the time window.

Every number is computed by the system from the store and pushed; the page never sums records itself and no agent ever types a figure (the SITREP lesson: build from records, check, send; tools/bearings/AGENTS.md SITREP section).

input.s: The Go service computes a counters view every tick over the store for four windows (1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d) and the previous window of each: tickets per stage (cut equals N-18 accepted, started equals N-07 dispatch, tested equals N-08 green, reviewed equals N-19 passed, merged equals N-09), seat bring-up seconds (N-15 seat.result bringup) as median and p95 with the design bound, stalls per node (N-12 stall records), records written per kind, jobs (N-24 pod.run), wakes (N-07 dispatch), seats (N-15 results), pods (N-24), cost (sum of seat.result cost and pod minutes), and the rail panel (N-33: steps done of total). N-31 pushes it as counters.frame when it changes (shared needs: shared/state-store.xml#view-counters and the counters.frame kind, declared in #shared-needs).

output.s: stats.frame is the drawn production panel; not stored. The client writes only its frame.report and a window.pref (the chosen window, per client, local storage, never a record).

panels.panel: Title Production, the window range in UTC, the window segment control 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d (primary action), and the stale chip.
Bar chart: cut, started, tested, reviewed, merged for the window and the previous window; one-line reading (for example "only 6 of 14 cut tickets reached merged; the line is on HOLD").
Median and p95 seat bring-up with the design bound as a dashed line and a sparkline of the last 12 seats.
Horizontal bars of stall records per node in the window; tap a bar opens that machine.
Records, jobs, wakes, seats, pods in the window with the previous window beside each.

Cost in the window: seat cost (subscription seats show turns and tokens, pod seats show the API cost, D03), pod minutes; the spend caps as lines: the per-ticket budget and the daily caps budget.daily_seat_usd and budget.daily_pod_minutes that N-07 enforces (shared/retry-budget.xml#budgets).
Steps done of total from the rail panel (N-33), ten cells, with the current step name.

mechanism.diagram: flowchart LR T[N-06 tick] --> CV[Go service: counters view over the store, four windows] CV --> CR[counters.frame record when changed] CR --> P[N-31 push] RL[N-33 rail.panel] --> P P --> C[client: stats module] C --> D[stats.frame drawn: bars, sparkline, counters, rail] C -->|change window| C C -->|tap a stall bar| SEL[selection record to N-39]

step.s: The counters view is SQL over the record tables grouped by kind and window, run on the tick; it writes a counters.frame record only when a value changed, keyed by window and the tick's UTC minute (idempotency key), so an idle line writes nothing. Placement inside the small Go cut is the G1 author's call (shared need).

The client subscribes to the counters view for the chosen window on the open stream (view counters, window 24h); changing the window changes the subscription; the previous window's frame stays drawn until the new one arrives, with the loading skeleton only on first open.

Charts are drawn on canvas with look.json tokens: bars in the production green #2BE327 for the window and the disabled grey #B3B3B3 for the previous window; the bound line in orange #FAA838; tech card icons from the atlas as legend markers (inventory section 5.3); numbers in IBM Plex Mono. No chart library (the bar is the Factorio production GUI, not a dashboard).
Tap a stall bar: a selection record for that node and the Machine screen; the window and the stats frame stay in the background.

states.state: Realistic volume for 24 h with a previous window, one longest-plausible node name in the stalls panel to expose truncation.
A window with no records: zero bars drawn as empty slots, the one-line explanation (no ticket moved in this window), and the primary recovery action as a real button: Widen the window to 7 d.
Skeleton bars and tiles matching the default layout; no centred spinner.
not-found (the counters view is absent, the Go service predates it), timeout (no frame within 10 s), validation (frame failed schema); what to do next and Retry.
Last counters stay drawn with the as-of stamp; the window control still works on the cached frames the client holds (all four windows are cached on receipt); no queued action exists on this screen.

start.s: The counters view runs on the Go tick; the push transport delivers it; the client subscribes on open. Ships in the N-38 bundle, promoted by N-48. No agent types or sums anything.

wait.name: counters-first-frame
wait.fallback: error state class timeout with Retry; automatic retry continues
wait.s: From the subscription to the first counters.frame.

wait.name: counters-staleness
wait.fallback: stale chip (503); at 10 min the offline banner; cached frames stay
wait.s: A counters.frame changes at most once per tick and may not change for minutes on an idle line, so the staleness bound is the tick heartbeat (N-31 idle heartbeat every 5 s keeps the stream alive; the frame's own at is what the stamp shows).

wait.name: counters-view-compute
wait.fallback: skip this tick's counters, record 504 counters.timeout once per hour at most, keep the previous frame
wait.s: The SQL over 7 d of records must finish inside the tick; the bound is measured and the query is indexed by kind and at (shared need: indexes).

wait.name: window-change
wait.fallback: show the cached frame for that window if any, else the loading skeleton then the timeout error

retries.s: Client steps retry 3 times with backoff then recover into a visible state; the counters view skipping a tick is reported, not retried inside the tick (the next tick is the retry); after three consecutive skipped ticks the Go service writes 500 counters.failed and N-28 builds one card.

many-agents.s: Readers: every client has its own window subscription; N clients on four windows are at most four distinct views the transport fans out; the counters view is computed once per tick regardless of client count.

Writers: only the Go service writes counters.frame, keyed by window and tick minute; two service instances overlapping during a restart produce a 409 on the second put that is dropped and logged. Clients write nothing but frame.report.

The counts are honest under concurrency: cut, started, tested, reviewed and merged count records by kind and at, never a running tally a seat maintains, so twenty seats finishing at once show as twenty records in the window.
Conflict detection: a counters.frame with a lower at than the one drawn is dropped; a frame whose window does not match the subscription is dropped and a full view requested.

status-codes.code: Frame failed schema on the client; full view requested; alert.
Three consecutive skipped ticks; one card.
No frame or heartbeat within the bound.
The counters query missed the tick bound; previous frame kept; at most one record per hour.

path.cleanup: N-45 retention class: keep 30 days of frames, then daily aggregates
lives in the owner's browser, not on the host; Reset view in the stamp menu clears it

permissions.s: Build seat: writes tools/map/src/stats/**, the Stats #panels of this volume, and tests; the counters view SQL and its tick hook are a G1 ticket against the Go service (shared need), never this seat's files.
Both keys read the screen; no action writes a record except a selection when a stall bar is tapped.

monitoring.s: The Stats screen is the system's own report on throughput; a 504 counters.timeout once an hour is tolerated and shown; three in a row is a card. The map draws N-40 as a machine whose lamp is the latest counters code.

runbook.s: Read the counters by hand (reading only): the Go service's gRPC Counters call with a window, or the dev tier's /events?view=counters&window=24h in a browser (nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views).
Cleanup: counters frames by N-45 retention; nothing on disk.
